actions.purpose: Page-by-page composition gap list: product versus prototype at three widths
actions.prompt:
In /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard (branch dashboard-0.33, the 0.33.0 dashboard as built) produce the composition gap list between the product and the approved prototype. Read docs/design/prototype-frames/README.md, then every file there: `<page>-120.txt` and `<page>-55.txt` are the exact prototype frames (and the `.tagged.txt` twins carry colour and click roles). [owner request, paraphrased] the product has the prototype's pages, tabs, keys and data but not its composition, density or colour: Home, Run, Stats overview, Budget and History each need a gap entry, and the prototype palette is missing almost everywhere. To see the product: `rm -rf /tmp/bsw-fid-home && mkdir -p /tmp/bsw-fid-home && cp -Rp ~/.bullswarm/workflows ~/.bullswarm/state.json ~/.bullswarm/meters ~/.bullswarm/providers.json /tmp/bsw-fid-home/ && BULLSWARM_HOME=/tmp/bsw-fid-home node /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard/bin/bullswarm.js workflow reindex`, then for each width W×H in 55×26, 120×40, 200×50: `tmux new-session -d -s fid -x W -y H "cd /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard && BULLSWARM_HOME=/tmp/bsw-fid-home CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=0 node bin/bullswarm.js"`, navigate with `tmux send-keys -t fid <key>` (r b s y f h, Tab, 1, Enter), read text with `tmux capture-pane -p -t fid`, and render colour to PNG with `python3 /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard/scripts/tui-shot.py fid out.png W H` (needs Pillow: `pip install pillow`). Never write to the real ~/.bullswarm.

For every page (Home, Runs, Run, Step, Budget, Stats × Overview/Trends/Pools/Models/Projects, History, Fleet, Help) and each width (55, 120, 200), put the product frame beside the prototype frame and record: (a) layout: columns, row order, section rules, what sits on the same row in the prototype but is stacked in the product, bar widths and where they are proportional; (b) density: rows the product spends on notes, wrapped sentences or repeated labels that the prototype does not; (c) colour: which elements the prototype colours (and how, from the tagged frames) and what the product paints, reading src/workflow/dash-kit.js, stats-view.js, budget-view.js, history-view.js, fleet-view.js and dashboard.js for the palette in use (Budget's meters already use #b6bd73/#e9c880/#bf6c69); (d) wording: labels the prototype uses that the product spells differently; (e) what the prototype shows that has no real source (keep the product's blank-plus-reason there). Then group the gaps into work territories by file with sizes S/M/L and name the shared modules (a palette in dash-kit, a column layout helper, a compact phone row helper) that several pages would need. Quote frames verbatim where you cite a gap. Others share this tree: preserve their edits and report any file you need outside your territory instead of editing it. Real data only: the prototype's numbers are illustrative; the product keeps its real figures and its ≈/basis rules; only the composition, density, colour and wording move to the prototype's.

actions.purpose: Author the fidelity goal and a validated program with per-page composition requirements and PNG-based acceptance
actions.prompt: In /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard, read the composition-gaps dependency output and docs/plans/dashboard-0.33.md, then write three files. 1) docs/plans/dashboard-0.33-fidelity.md: the gap list condensed into work items with exact files, sizes and territories. 2) docs/plans/dashboard-0.33-fidelity.goal.txt: the goal for the fidelity workflow, under 25 lines, one numbered requirement per page (Home, Run and Step, Budget, Stats overview and trends, Stats pools/models/projects, History, Fleet and Help) phrased as "matches the prototype frame's composition, density and colour at 55, 120 and 200 columns while keeping real data and the ≈/basis rules", plus one for the shared palette and layout helpers, one for the phone layouts, one for tests, and one for docs/changelog. 3) docs/plans/dashboard-0.33-fidelity.program.json in the format of docs/reference/program.md (read it): first a shared-kit territory (palette, column layout, compact phone rows in src/workflow/dash-kit.js and its test) that page writers depend on; then parallel implement writers, one per page family, each owning exact files (no directories or globs, no two writers on one file; src/workflow/dashboard.js stays one territory); a digest if three or more outputs feed one reader; one integration action with ownedFiles []; one adversarial-acceptance action with evidenceFor covering every requirement whose prompt says: render every page at 55×26, 120×40 and 200×50 with scripts/tui-shot.py against a fixture home (To see the product: `rm -rf /tmp/bsw-fid-home && mkdir -p /tmp/bsw-fid-home && cp -Rp ~/.bullswarm/workflows ~/.bullswarm/state.json ~/.bullswarm/meters ~/.bullswarm/providers.json /tmp/bsw-fid-home/ && BULLSWARM_HOME=/tmp/bsw-fid-home node /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard/bin/bullswarm.js workflow reindex`, ), place each PNG and text capture beside the prototype frame and screenshot, and judge composition, density and colour, not the presence of features. Every prompt is self-contained, names /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard, the prototype frame files to match, the exact files owned, the capture commands, tests to add and `npm test` with the summary quoted, and ends with: Others share this tree: preserve their edits and report any file you need outside your territory instead of editing it. Real data only: the prototype's numbers are illustrative; the product keeps its real figures and its ≈/basis rules; only the composition, density, colour and wording move to the prototype's. Validate with `bullswarm workflow plan validate "$(cat /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard/docs/plans/dashboard-0.33-fidelity.goal.txt)" --cwd=/home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard --program=/home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard/docs/plans/dashboard-0.33-fidelity.program.json --json`; fix issues until exit 0 and quote the advisories; do not launch. Others share this tree: preserve their edits and report any file you need outside your territory instead of editing it. Real data only: the prototype's numbers are illustrative; the product keeps its real figures and its ≈/basis rules; only the composition, density, colour and wording move to the prototype's.
